agent: Claude Code (CLAUDE.md, this repository) — WP-03a verification: item (vi), ClaimsPort.renew sub-finding
summary_for_principal:
This closes another sub-part of the same checklist item as several earlier PRs (settings the system accepts but doesn't fully act on).

Re-checking the specific claim (a reuse-safety mechanism sits unused) turned up something more serious underneath: the mechanism it depends on was never switched on for the important case. When a step performs a real side effect and hands off to an external worker, the system should record 'someone is already doing this' so a racing second attempt waits rather than duplicating the side effect. That recording never happened for hand-off work — only for work the system does immediately in-process, which barely needs it.

Fixed the more important half: a hand-off now gets the same protection immediate work always had. Renewing that protection if the external work runs long still needs a new capability this system can't ask for yet, and building it would mean guessing at something the spec doesn't describe. I've written that up rather than guess.

Full test suite: 383 passed, 1 new.

Numbered actions:
1. Nothing needs deciding right now.
2. One sub-part of this item remains, the last piece of WP-03a's original work.

also.reason: New regression test proving a hand-off Tool now acquires a claim (a second next() call on the same run/scope returns STEP_RUNNING instead of a fresh TOOL_STEP), confirmed failing before the fix.

lessons.maxim: When re-verifying an earlier report's finding, trace the actual call graph one level deeper than the report's own framing before deciding a fix's scope — the reported symptom (a method never called) can be a downstream consequence of a more fundamental, more consequential gap (the method's own prerequisite never happening either) that the original framing didn't distinguish.
lessons.incident: The original item (vi) sub-finding named only 'ClaimsPort.renew never called' — true, but tracing ctx.claims.acquire's own call sites directly found it was itself only ever invoked for one of two dispatch paths, making the hand-off case (the more consequential one for real-world side effects) entirely unprotected, not merely un-renewable.

lessons.proposed_check: When a reported finding names 'X is never called', check not only whether X is called, but whether X's own prerequisite (the thing that would make calling X meaningful) is itself correctly wired everywhere it should be.
